tested_revision: working tree on top of c31ba09 (round-4 fixes: validator reads input-log, observation-time cancellation rule, guard-failure receipt, agent-driven manual input; committed with this receipt)

criteria.expected: no gameplay input, paused receipt, stop_requested latched
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=0 presses=0; input-log records stop_requested at t=0.001 (detection latency 0.001 s) and no press records
criteria.negative_control: pre-gate runtime classifies before checking the stop file; the latch now happens in run() via _stop_check before any classification

criteria.expected: wait exits; zero recovery B/route writes after observation
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=1 presses=20; STOP lands during turn 2's post-route wait; stop event at t<60 s; no late key writes
criteria.negative_control: Astra round-3 repro: pre-fix runtime sent B plus a full re-drive after observing STOP (reproduced as the strict-press scenario's first failing run)

criteria.expected: remaining route keys suppressed; at least one press aborted; zero writes after observation
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=0 presses=5 (vs 20+ pre-gate); ABORTED-press record present; zero key writes timestamped after stop_requested in the RAW write stream (observation-time rule, not run() return); stop event prompt
criteria.negative_control: first run of this scenario on the pre-fix code reproduced Astra's exact escaped-press shape (recorded in docs/project-log.md 2026-09-17 round-3 entry)

criteria.expected: remaining recovery inputs suppressed; no press/drive record starts after stop_requested
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=2 presses=65; STOP dropped on the first recovery B write; zero key writes timestamped after stop_requested in the RAW write stream (round-4 gap 2: the rule is measured from STOP observation, not run() return, so a write escaping before return cannot hide)
criteria.negative_control: pre-round-3 recovery checked the stop file only after press+drive; the loop now checks before each input and press() returns -1 on abort

criteria.command: python tools/validate_transport_paths.py --scenario strict-press --out-root outputs/autobattle (evidence-window retry loop shares wait_progress stop_check with all supplemental waits)
criteria.observed: wait_progress threads stop_check into its inner pump (stop_when per packet cycle); all runtime waits pass self._stop_check; paused state reached in every stop scenario
criteria.negative_control: pre-fix supplemental wait (seconds=5.0, min_new_seeds=9999999) had no stop_check parameter at all

criteria.expected: cancellation wins; no new turn starts after the latched stop
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=0; STOP dropped as the first post-commit seed arrived; no turn event after stop_requested; detection latency 0.19 s after the stop_when fix (was 2.997-3.005 s, over the 2 s bound)
criteria.negative_control: pre-stop_when code measured 3.005 s detection latency (one full 3 s pump tick), over the contract bound; recorded in the limitations of the prior working tree

criteria.expected: actual CLI/finally/__exit__ keeps owned PID alive, disarms owned hooks, releases keys, detaches
criteria.observed: probe reproduces the CLI's exact finally semantics (flip session.keep_process BEFORE __exit__): emulator pid survived __exit__ (probe.json emulator_survived=true), breakpoints disarmed in _finish, no key writes owned (per-press scratch re-write), transport closed
criteria.negative_control: Astra's round-2 mocked-CLI repro: __exit__ still called stop()'s kill default because keep_process never reached the session

criteria.expected: actual cleanup terminates ONLY the owned process
criteria.observed: run reached a bounded terminal state (stalled after the tracked player fell; 3 turns), keep_process=False reached __exit__, owned pid 23268 terminated, port released; no other process touched (taskkill scoped to the owned pid inside stop())
criteria.negative_control: the leave-running variant with the same code path survives, proving the flag and not an accident decides the outcome

criteria.command: python tools/validate_transport_paths.py --scenario disconnect --out-root outputs/autobattle; python tools/validate_transport_paths.py --scenario guard-failure --out-root outputs/autobattle; guard failure observed live 2026-09-15 (a3 first-boot, name decode failure)
criteria.expected: no further gameplay input; truthful terminal reason AND a complete receipt on the guard-failure path (Astra round 4 gap 3: the CLI exited before writing run.json and passed a `reason` kwarg the event schema drops)
criteria.observed: disconnect: state=connection_lost, stop event records 'transport lost', zero presses after failure; guard-failure scenario drives the REAL run_autobattle.main() with the faked session: exit code 1, run.json written on the guard-failure path (final_state=stalled, turns=0), the failure reason rides the stop event note, a start event precedes the stop so the lifecycle validator accepts the receipt, and no input records exist
criteria.negative_control: pre-fix CLI returned before any receipt and emitted stop with a dropped `reason` kwarg; the scenario's first run failed exactly that way (missing run.json + 4 accumulated stop events)

criteria.expected: emulator survives cleanup AND a manual player command visibly works on the handed-off battle (Astra round 4: agent-driven player input through the window is sufficient; no human required)
criteria.observed: runner paused at turns=1, keep_process=True reached the real __exit__, emulator pid survived; the agent then sent player input through the WINDOW (SendInput: START,DOWN,DOWN - the mGBA keyboard bindings, never the GDB stub); the screen visibly changed (manual-before.png vs manual-after.png differ) and the stub write log shows zero writes after handoff (20 before = 20 after), so the detached session did not fight the player
criteria.negative_control: the stub key-write count is sampled at handoff and after player input: any post-handoff stub write would mean the detached runner still drove input (fought the player) and fail the probe

criteria.expected: STOP observed within 2 s outside an already-pending OS/transport call
criteria.observed: stop-before-start 0.001 s; stop-during-recovery 1.185 s; stop-coincides-with-progress 0.19 s (after the stop_when fix); latency = observation time minus stop-file mtime
criteria.negative_control: measured 3.005 s (over bound) before the per-packet-cycle stop_when fix; left in project log as the failing case

live_runs.result: PASS kill: owned pid 79864 terminated, port released (rerun on final round-4 code)
PASS manual input: agent-driven player input via window visibly worked; zero stub writes after handoff

limitations: offline scenarios certify control flow and ordering with a scripted engine; the fake mirrors recorded shapes (commit-then-effects, key-poll-per-frame) but ROM semantics of individual bytes are outside C1's scope
transport reads inside press() use blocking socket timeouts (~0.2 s per packet); STOP observed there waits for the press cycle to finish (~1.2 s), within the 2 s bound
the manual-input proof uses START/DOWN (menu/cursor) rather than a tactical command: C2's identified-action selector is the packet that proves deliberate tactical selection end to end
